tasks.short: Prepare and deliver criminal justice lectures

steps.what: Select lecture objectives, verified sources and teaching examples
Prepare lecture materials and verify explanations against current sources

loop.purpose: Draft lecture structure and explanatory examples
loop.check: Lecturer checks legal meaning, jurisdiction, dates and pedagogical suitability against original sources
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported passages are rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations and teaching examples require contextual writing rather than fixed field substitution

steps.what: Deliver lectures and respond to students' questions

tasks.design: Use a bounded drafting helper within {DOCS} for lecturer-selected material. The lecturer checks every substantive explanation before retaining the exact final version and delivers the lecture personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lecture drafting involves contextual explanation and examples.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded text draft can be checked against a small source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Current law, sensitive policing examples and student understanding require expert judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining difficult distinctions and adapting to the room.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation gain can support additional worked examples; teaching responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Learning outcome alignment and accessible presentation

evidence.claim: Source-bounded text drafting can assist lecture preparation, but these time assumptions are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers preparation and delivery of one lecture; syllabus creation, assessment and later advising are separate.

Lecturer produces objectives, audience level, jurisdiction, source versions and permitted examples in s1, with capture time included. Missing sources mean manual preparation; no generated legal updates are accepted.
Test native document templates and approved drafting features before custom code.
Student questions arise live; no transcription, automatic student profiling or structured question feed is assumed.
unknowns: Availability of approved current teaching sources
research_questions: Can checked drafts reduce preparation without increasing legal corrections or weakening explanations?

incremental.description: Maintaining source restrictions and reviewing failed drafts

approvals.approved_version: Final lecture text, examples and source versions; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=93.75, gross=6.25, focal upkeep=4, net=2.25. Range allows extensive legal checking to consume the benefit; live delivery retains 55 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions, challenging reasoning and balancing participation

tasks.design: Keep discussion facilitation with the lecturer. Existing prompts in {DOCS} can support the session, but live moderation has no established removable clerical component.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is responding to people in context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing teaching materials remain available without a new system.
tasks.still_hard: Handling contentious topics and unequal participation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertainty, discomfort and teachable disagreement.
tasks.altitude: No change to the teaching week or decision rights.

evidence.claim: Classroom moderation depends on live interpersonal and subject judgement; no labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the live classroom discussion; lecture materials and assessment are counted separately.
Students produce contributions in the session; no structured transcript or sentiment input is assumed.
Consider native teaching features before custom software; no automation is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because facilitation and existing materials remain unchanged.
research_questions: Is any administrative work actually part of these discussions rather than another task?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Live discussions remain fully counted, including difficult exchanges.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read assignments and papers against the assessment rubric
Write feedback from marker notes and rubric findings

loop.purpose: Draft feedback from the lecturer's own findings
loop.input: Marker notes, rubric findings and selected submission passages
loop.check: Lecturer checks that comments accurately express the findings, refer to actual passages and suggest appropriate revisions
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported or misleading comments are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Expressing individual feedback requires contextual prose rather than a fixed rubric label

steps.what: Evaluate final grades, correct feedback and release the assessed work

tasks.design: Use {LMS} to draft feedback from the lecturer's marker notes. Keep reading, grade decisions and final release with the lecturer, including any required separate grade record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning assessment findings into useful individual comments takes writing time.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based feedback drafting is an available capability.
tasks.still_hard: Legal reasoning, fairness and meaningful feedback need subject expertise.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a weak argument from an unconventional defensible one.
tasks.altitude: Limited feedback drafting assistance leaves grade authority unchanged.

reach.task: Improve feedback patterns for common reasoning errors

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
The proposed writing reduction and upkeep are unmeasured task assumptions, not observed grading results.

assumptions: Boundary covers coursework and papers; examination scripts belong to the separate examination task.

Lecturer produces rubric item, finding, passage reference and intended advice in s1; note capture remains fully counted. Students submit work through the existing process, which is not changed or credited as a saving.
Native approved feedback drafting is tested before custom integration. Missing or unusable notes mean manual feedback.
No automatic grades, misconduct findings or silent grade synchronization; required additional records remain in s3.
unknowns: Whether feedback is already generated from notes
Permission to process submissions in the approved environment
research_questions: Does editing note-based drafts take less time than writing comments at equivalent quality?

incremental.description: Rubric prompt upkeep and review of drafting failures

approvals.approved_version: Student, submission version, rubric, grade and final feedback; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=93.75, gross=6.25 minus focal upkeep4 gives net2.25. Range allows difficult papers and extensive feedback corrections; reading and grade decisions retain their full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Compile examinations, approve answer keys and administer the assessment
Score closed examination questions against the approved answer key
Grade open examinations, review anomalies and release final results

tasks.design: Configure closed-question scoring in {LMS} from an examiner-approved key. The lecturer retains examination construction, administration, open-answer marking, anomaly resolution and final release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly checking fixed answers against a key consumes marking effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native closed-question marking can apply explicit answer rules.
tasks.still_hard: Test validity and judging open legal reasoning.
tasks.human_edge: Evaluating defensible alternative answers and responding to flawed questions.
tasks.altitude: Spend a small share of marking time examining weak items and disputed responses.

evidence.claim: Ans auto-marks closed questions and provides item statistics.
The task shares and proposed net saving are E1 assumptions, conditional on manually scored closed questions existing today.

assumptions: Boundary covers examinations only, excluding coursework and papers in the other grading task.

Lecturer produces examination version, item IDs, accepted answers, points and roster mapping in s1; candidate response capture occurs during retained administration. Students answer through the existing exam process; no new student work is introduced.
Missing key fields, ambiguous responses or failed submission imports are marked manually in s3. No structured correctness flag is assumed without an approved key.
Test native assessment configuration first. Existing automated scoring earns no new saving; capture and exam administration remain counted.
unknowns: Existing examination software and permitted result exports
research_questions: What fraction of current marking consists of fixed-key questions that are not already automatically scored?

already_counted.description: Key creation and administration including capture
Anomaly review, open marking and release

incremental.description: Key regression tests and scoring configuration upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Candidate, exam and key versions, item scores, open marks and final result; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross20 minus focal upkeep8 gives net12. Zero when scoring is already automatic or exams contain no fixed-key questions; modest range allows import and key exceptions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retains teaching and assessment authority while testing bounded preparation and marking support.
reach: Help instructional designers improve examples and examination items
role.ambitious_version: Use measured preparation gains to provide clearer explanations and more useful feedback without weakening assessment judgement.

job.title: Criminal Justice and Law Enforcement Teachers, Postsecondary
